## Images

`hero.png` and `checker.png` are generated byte for byte by `make-fixtures.mjs` in this directory,
using only `node:zlib` and a hand-written PNG chunk encoder — no image library and no source image
are involved. Regenerate them with:

```sh
node tests/fixtures/assets/2d/make-fixtures.mjs
```

| File          | Bytes | Size  | Content                                                                             | SHA-256                                                            |
| ------------- | ----- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `hero.png`    | 164   | 64×64 | A 2×2 grid of 32×32 flat-colour frames in reading order: red, green, blue, yellow.  | `31bc38311fa995f1be86562d2497e4829433f05020633d5d24aa4a9728d37ee7` |
| `checker.png` | 91    | 16×16 | A one-pixel magenta/black checkerboard; the S6.3 pixel-perfect spike reads it back. | `b40f3079967758c2c0b11091bc2bb7ee3d351cb964fbb950d1ea90e26e069b18` |

The frame colours are far apart in every channel so a screenshot assertion can identify a frame
from a single texel, and each frame is a flat colour so its own one-pixel border is identical to
its interior — an extruded border by construction, which is what the pixel-perfect import check
(`IGX-1102`) wants to see.

## Documents

`hero.atlas.json`, `hero.spriteanim.json`, `sample.tmj`, and `sample.ldtk` were hand-written for
these tests.

- `hero.atlas.json` (`ignifx.spriteatlas`) and `hero.spriteanim.json` (`ignifx.spriteanimation`)
  are ignifx's own formats, documented in `docs/architecture/06-serialization-and-scene-format.md`
  §6.
- `sample.tmj` is a Tiled orthogonal map written by hand against the published
  [Tiled JSON map format](https://doc.mapeditor.org/en/stable/reference/json-map-format/)
  (`"version": "1.10"`). It carries a 4×4 `Ground` tile layer whose bottom-left 3×2 tiles are
  solid, one one-way tile, one animated tile, and an object layer with one `spawn` object — the
  shapes the importer and the collision merger are tested on. No file produced by the Tiled editor
  was used.
- `sample.ldtk` is an LDtk project written by hand against the published
  [LDtk JSON format](https://ldtk.io/json/) (`"jsonVersion": "1.5.3"`), describing the same 4×4
  level through a `Tiles` layer, an `IntGrid` collision layer, and an `Entities` layer. No file
  produced by the LDtk editor was used, and no LDtk sample project was copied.

Both editor formats are documentation, not code: reading a published format specification and
writing a conforming document by hand creates no derivative work of either editor.

`checker.atlas.json` and `checker-linear.atlas.json` are the same one-frame document over
`checker.png`, differing only in `sampling` (`nearest` and `linear`). Spike S6.3 renders both: the
`nearest` one through a pixel-perfect camera to prove the checker stays crisp, and the `linear` one
at a deliberately fractional zoom as the counter-example that shows what the flag prevents.
